svg.title: Longer steps shrink the region where a fixed point stays stable
svg.desc: Conceptual diagram with toy values, not measured data. Left: the complex plane with three nested disks that all touch the point 1: the unit disk for step 1, a dashed disk of radius 0.8 for step 1.25, and a disk of radius 0.5 for step 2. Two toy multipliers sit on the real axis: -0.6, which lies exactly on the boundary of the step-1.25 disk, and 0.9, which lies inside all three. Right: for a step lambda, a multiplier stays inside the unit circle only within a disk of radius 1/lambda touching 1; the multiplier -0.6 reaches the circle at -1 at step 1.25, 25 percent longer than the unrelaxed step 1; the multiplier 0.9, near +1, slows settling but stays inside every disk drawn, and its edge is at step 20, so here the slowest multiplier does not set the edge. Footer: the edge is set by the multiplier the shrinking disk reaches first, which need not be the largest one.
svg.text: The stability edge: how far a step can grow
Toy multipliers on the complex plane; not a measured spectrum.
